sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.2% a year from FY2016 to FY2025 [F157], but the shape is one peak and a decline, not a steady climb.
Revenue peaked at $61.3 billion in FY2023 [F8] and fell to $45.7 billion by FY2025 [F10].
The FY2018 revenue increase of 25.6% [D93] followed the Wirtgen acquisition, which added 12 percent to net sales [P72].
Operating income rose 86.1% in FY2021 [D232] as the cost of sales ratio fell, mainly on price realization [P45].
Production and Precision Agriculture was 38.9% of FY2025 revenue [D867] and fell 17.0% [D868], taking 7.0pp off group growth [D869].
The FY2025 filing cites a 30% drop in U.S. and Canada sales volumes, partly offset by 22% growth in Brazil [P10].
Financial Services grew 23.5% in FY2024 [D1096] and added 1.7pp to group growth [D1097], as average wholesale receivables rose 26 percent [P14].
Operating income fell 30.2% in FY2024 [D368], more than the 15.6% revenue drop [D367], so profit deleveraged on the way down.
Diluted EPS compounded at 16.1% a year [F162] against 14.2% for net income [F160], helped by a share count that fell from 316.6 million to 271.7 million [X110][X119].
FY2024 operating margin of 17.5% [F30] sits above the 12.1% window median [D1335] and below the 21.2% FY2023 high [D1334]; FY2025 operating income is not in the pack.
Operating margin fell 3.7pp in FY2024 [D378], with SG&A accounting for 1.9pp [D391] and R&D for 0.9pp [D390].
The filing says production costs were favourable on lower material costs, partly offset by higher overhead from lower volumes [P16].
The FY2021 margin gain of 6.1pp [D243] came mainly from price realization, with lower SG&A after 2020 separation costs [P45].
The FY2018 tax rate of 42.4% [D81] included a $704 million tax reform charge [P72], so that year's net margin of 6.3% [F43] understates operations.
FY2025 free cash flow was $6.10 billion [F100], or 1.21x net income [D402], against a 0.91x window median [D1347].
The filing credits FY2025 operating cash flow to net income adjusted for non-cash items and lower receivables, less an OPEB contribution [P5].
Conversion fell to 0.66x in FY2022 [D266] on higher receivables and inventories and a $1.00 billion OPEB contribution [P27].
Capex was 3.0% of FY2025 revenue [D397] and 0.61x D&A [D403], down from 0.77x in FY2024 [D358].
Net cash was -$5.52 billion in FY2025 [D407], or -12.1% of revenue [D408], ranking at the 100th percentile of seven industrials peers [D1357] against a -38.8% median [D1358].
The filing says the two businesses are capitalised differently and use separate metrics [P3], so consolidated net cash mixes the two.
FY2025 buybacks and dividends totalled $2.86 billion, 46.9% of free cash flow [D409][D410], as diluted shares fell 1.9% [D427].
The total-debt series falls from $43.8 billion in FY2021 [D225] to $12.6 billion in FY2022 [D271], so I do not compare debt across that break.
Revenue fell in FY2024 and FY2025, from $51.7 billion [F9] to $45.7 billion [F10], a 3-year CAGR of -4.6% [D1348].
The FY2024 filing ties lower shipments to rising grain stocks, lower commodity prices and elevated interest rates [P17].
Production and Precision Agriculture is 38.9% of revenue [D867] and fell 21.7% in FY2024 [D865] before falling 17.0% in FY2025 [D868].
The provision for credit losses rose to $296 million in FY2025 [X171] from -$16.0 million in FY2023 [X169], as delinquencies rose in agriculture and turf accounts [P4].
Construction and Forestry operating margin fell to 8.8% in FY2025 [D1319] from 18.0% in FY2023 [D1317], and the pack holds no FY2025 cause for it.
Free cash flow margin was 13.4% in FY2025 [D398]; a fall toward the 11.6% window median [D1341] would confirm the lower operating cash flow guided for 2026 [P6], per the FY2026 10-K.
The provision for credit losses was $296 million in FY2025 [X171]; a figure above the $310 million FY2024 level [X170] would confirm deterioration, per the FY2026 10-K.

Production and Precision Agriculture operating margin was 15.0% in FY2025 [D1309] against 21.1% in FY2024 [D1308]; a recovery toward the FY2024 level would signal stabilising volumes, per the FY2026 10-K.
